sense: degree of an adjective or adverb

evidence: Quint. 1.5.45: huic partī subjungātur licet per comparātiōnēs et superlātiōnēs
terms.comment: Quintilian’s word for comparative forms, beside superlātiō for superlatives. In the comparative is comparātīvē or in comparātiōne (Traupman 245).

evidence: Don. p. 1745 P. (Lewis & Short s.v. comparātīvus)
terms.comment: The later grammarians’ gradus comparātīvus, or the adjective alone: doctior (Traupman 232).

phrases.latin: similiter in vocābulīs et nōminibus fit soloecismus genere, numerō, propriē autem cāsibus … huic partī subjungātur licet per comparātiōnēs et superlātiōnēs
phrases.english: likewise in nouns a mistake is made in gender, number and above all case … to this part one may add mistakes in comparatives and superlatives

sources: Lewis & Short: comparatio · Lewis & Short: comparativus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 232, p. 245.
